text:
harper: hey all, day 2 q's — I keep getting a 403 when I try to open the Redwood Console (prod). Also trying to run e2e in CI and we need a service account and the owner for the feature flag 'signup_beta'. who do I ping for flag ownership and what's the fastest path to a CI SA?

julia: welcome harper :wave: do you see the SSO prompt or a straight 403? first thing: try incognito or clear cookies, then sign in with SSO. sometimes group sync is delayed. if it's still 403, paste the exact error screenshot and i'll check group membership. docs: https://redwood.internal/onboarding/access (use 'Request console access' section)

samir: if you want a quick check for your groups, run: `curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" https://console.redwood/api/v1/me` and look for `groups` in the JSON. (replace $TOKEN with the one from the console dev token page). also make sure you're hitting the right environment — staging vs prod have different org ids.

harper: it shows SSO then right away 403. i tried incognito — same. screenshot attached. can't access the FF panel to check owner.

julia: ok i'll look. @maya can you confirm if new-hires group synced?

maya: just checked — your account exists but not in `console-admins` nor `feature-owners`. i can grant temporary staging-admin for 4 hours to unblock you, but prod FF ownership needs an owner person added. if you need to change flags in a PR we can do a guarded change on your behalf. do you need prod write or just to see owner metadata?

harper: need owner info + a SA for CI to toggle flags for e2e runs. prod read-only would be ok for now.

infra-bot: Access request created: INC-9234. Requester: harper. Requested roles: console-read, temporary-staging-admin (4h). ETA for manual review: ~30m.

maya: i've granted `console-read` in prod so you should be able to see the FF panel now. if you still can't, logout/login once.

harper: can now see the FF list — thanks! owner is listed as `product-bob`. who owns CI SAs?

julia: for CI service accounts we use the internal service-account workflow — open the `Service Account Request` form (link in onboarding docs) and include: team, repo, intended use, TTL (recommended 30d), and whether it needs KMS access. tag `infra` and `security` in the request. sample command we use for GCP-based SAs (example only): `gcloud iam service-accounts create redwood-ci-<team> --display-name=\"CI runner\"` but don't run anything until infra approves.

samir: if your CI is ephemeral (e.g., GitHub Actions) ask for token-based short-lived creds. for persistent Jenkins runners we provision a SA and rotate keys. include the repo path and the person on-call for the pipeline in the request.

harper: filed INC-9234 comment with repo and TTL. also pinged product-bob about flag ownership. thanks everyone!

maya: quick note — product-bob is OOO until Thu but product-alex is deputy for flags; ping them if you need a faster sign-off. i'll follow up on the SA request once infra triages INC-9234.

harper: awesome, this unblocks my e2e work. appreciate the speedy help :heart:

julia: welcome again — shout if you hit anything else, and i'll drop a short checklist PM with the common console gotchas.

maya: closing loop — temporary staging admin will auto-revoke in 4 hours. if you need longer, we can extend after approvals.

harper: noted. thanks y'all!
